gaps.note: dell/riser-divider-plate-14g@1's OUTLINE AND DEPTH ARE MEASURED and its FACE IS NOT. Both bodies come off Dell's service model to the hundredth - face 267.32..278.64 and 297.10..308.42, y 1.81..42.42, 17.61 proud - but what is printed or punched on them has not been established from any figure. Riser 1's equivalent plate carries a five-slot column that appears in no cut of the model at any plane and had to be read off ISM figure 8; whether these two carry the same column, or anything else, was NOT SEARCHED FOR rather than looked for and found absent. The recess drawn for the card clip is drawn because a clip sits in a recess on riser 1, not because this plate was seen to have one.
gaps.wanted: a rear photograph or ISM figure at usable resolution across face 267..309, which would settle both plates at once - they are the same pressing

gaps.note: WHICH OF THE TWO IS IN FRONT IS ASSERTED, NOT MEASURED. dell/riser-1-top- shelf-14g@1 is 14.68 proud (measured, the chassis shell's front) and dell/riser-1-shroud-14g@1's plate is extruded at 17.76 (an approximation across a whole outline, as that file's depth key says), so the plate drew in front and the shelf read as tucked under the piece it closes the top of. The operator, looking at the render against the hardware, says the shelf is the outermost thing there. It is expressed as a 3.10 `lift` on the composition - the smallest value that clears 17.76 - so both measured depths survive untouched and only the ordering changes. If the plate's width and depth are ever settled properly (see riser-1-shroud-rib-width-unresolved, which is the same piece of missing evidence) this lift should be re-derived rather than kept.
gaps.wanted: a mechanical drawing or a caliper on the hardware giving the riser-1 shroud plate's front and the chassis top shelf's front at the same face x, which is the one measurement that settles the ordering outright

gaps.note: THE MID BAYS ARE NOT NUMBERED HERE, AND THAT IS DELIBERATE. This device numbers its front drives 0 to 23 and its rear drives 12 to 15 or 24 to 27, in both cases because Dell's own label says so and the numbering was checked against it. NOTHING FOUND SO FAR SAYS WHAT DELL CALLS THE FOUR MID-BAY DRIVES. They are `mid-lff-0..3` and `mid-sff-0..3`, which are positions and not claims: they say "the four slots, left to right" and assert nothing about what the machine prints or what iDRAC reports. Inventing a range that looked like the others - 24 to 27 say - would have been the easy thing and would have been a fabrication of exactly the kind the front and rear numbering was careful to avoid.
gaps.wanted: the mid-drive-tray page of the R740xd installation and service manual, or a photograph of the tray with its silkscreen legible

gaps.note: THE PREVIOUS FORM OF THIS GAP SAID THE CAD POSE WAS EXPLODED. IT IS NOT, AND THE SENTENCE IS KEPT HERE BECAUSE IT IS THE INSTRUCTIVE PART. A reading of R740XD_GPU_Brackets_01-1 was rejected on the grounds that its y extent ran -40 to +24 against an 86.8 mm panel - "not a seated pose". That was a Y-CONVENTION ARTEFACT IN THE READER, not a fact about the model. Calibrated against the rear handle, whose device y is trusted, the convention is face_y = 86.8 - raw_y; it reproduces the handle's low edge at 42.35 to the hundredth and this assembly's own sibling R740XD_Expansioncard_Clip-1.001 at y 1.81..44.81, the figure riser-1-shroud-14g already carried from an independent read. The pose is seated and the 36.9 mm was real all along - a plausibility check that fires on the reader instead of the data rejects good evidence, and it cost a wrong fix at the other end of the part. WHAT THE MODEL ACTUALLY SHOWS, descended to mesh children, is two levels: Body_2_3.002 at 111.70..148.60, 11.06 proud - a wide lower shelf, now drawn - and Body_1_3.005 at 125.00..135.10, 17.71 proud - a narrow rib. WHAT IS STILL OPEN is the rib. riser-1-shroud-14g draws it 120.64..137.26, about 4 mm wider on each side than the body at that depth. The outline came from cad-outline.py cutting at the panel plane, which returns the SILHOUETTE of everything the plane crosses rather than one body, so it cannot settle a single body's width. Re-cutting it would move the slot column and the clip recess, both photo-measured off ISM figure 8 and both currently agreeing with the render, so it is recorded rather than guessed.
gaps.wanted: a mechanical drawing of the riser-1 shroud, or a clean section of R740XD_GPU_Brackets_01-1 above the shelf, to settle the raised rib's width independently of the panel-plane silhouette

gaps.note: THE NUMBER CAME FROM A DESCRIPTION, NOT A MEASUREMENT. std/vga@1 stands 6.73 proud because that is what a D-sub does when its flange bolts through sheet metal, and on this machine's front the connector is on the control panel board, which sits back from the bezel - so only a little of it emerges. The operator, looking at the hardware, put that at "a millimetre and a half"; `inset: 5.23` is 6.73 less 1.50 and is therefore an estimate dressed as two decimal places. IT IS THE SETBACK THAT IS UNKNOWN, not the connector. The 6.73 is TE 114-40010's mating dimension and stays; what nobody here has measured is how far behind the faceplate the board sits. A caliper on the hardware, or any drawing that dimensions the control panel board against the front bezel, replaces one number and nothing else. THE REAR D-SUBS ARE NOT AFFECTED. They bolt through the rear panel in the ordinary way and carry no inset.
gaps.wanted: the control panel board's setback from the front bezel, measured

gaps.note: TWO NUMBERS, ONE APPEARANCE EACH, AND NEITHER CORROBORATED. This device seats both supplies at y 46.20, and the only other place that number appears is a comment on riser 2's plate saying the plate was cut back to "face 46.20 - the power supply's top edge", which cites this seating rather than a source. psu-1100w-ac-14g's provenance used to argue the module top was y 45.0, read off R740 ISM figure 9 - but it argued that in the same breath as a height of 41.8, and the height has since been measured off Dell's own service model at 39.1. A position argued from a reading whose companion number is disproven is not evidence for the position. THE CAD CANNOT ANSWER IT. glb-parts.py states the rule it enforces: sizes survive a pose and positions do not, and this scene draws the supply with its withdrawal handle swung open for a removal procedure. The body measures cleanly at 86.3 x 39.1 x 195.5 and its face y lands nowhere near either candidate. AN ATTEMPT TO RE-READ FIGURE 9 FAILED GATE 1 AT 13.18%, against a provenance that claims 0.26% for the same figure - so the failure is in the panel detection, not in the figure, and nothing may be taken off it until somebody finds the body's true top and bottom edges in that raster. The seating is left where it is rather than moved on a measurement that did not pass its own gate. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: the body edges in ISM figure 9 identified by hand rather than by ink-density, which turns the 13.18% back into the 0.26% the figure is capable of and makes the fraction readable. 1.2 mm is worth one careful pass, because riser 2's plate is cut to this number.
gaps.wanted: the supply's top edge on the rear face, from a figure that has passed Gate 1

gaps.note: Dell's model carries riser 1 (three-slot, measured here to the tenth) and the low-profile riser 2C. It carries no full-height riser 2 and no riser 3. Their bodies - the PCB and the slot connectors in `body.boxes` on dell/riser-2a/2d/2e/2f-14g and dell/riser-3a/3b-14g - are riser 1's, stood at their own bays' outer edges, and riser 3's PCB is cut to end at the supply cage it stands on.
gaps.wanted: A model or a photograph of riser 2A and riser 3 seated, which would put both PCBs where they are.

gaps.note: ISM figures 17 and 18 number five fronts - 24, 16 and 8 x 2.5 inch at bays 0-23, 0-15 and 0-7, and 12 and 8 x 3.5 inch at 0-11 and 0-7. TWO OF THE FIVE ARE NOW DRAWN. `front` is the 24 x 2.5 inch; `front-lff-12` is the 12 x 3.5 inch, the one that mattered, because it is the front the rears numbered 12-15 and 12-13 belong to. It is a variant view with `face: front`, bound by the `lff12-` configurations, and its grid was measured off dellr740xd-12x35.webp at Gate 1 0.07% - the same backplane opening the 24 SFF bays divide, 428.832 / 4 = 107.208 against a measured period of 107.216. THE 16 AND 8 x 2.5 INCH AND THE 8 x 3.5 INCH ARE STILL NOT MODELLED, and no figure for them has been measured.
gaps.wanted: the remaining three fronts as further `face: front` variants, each with a configuration to bind it.

gaps.note: DELL ENUMERATES THEM. ISM table 28, "Supported backplane options for PowerEdge R740XD systems", lists front, mid and rear together - ten rows, and the coupling falls straight out: 2.5in x24 no rear 2.5in x24 + 2.5in x4 mid + 2.5in x4 rear 2.5in x24 (20 SAS/SATA + 4 NVMe) no rear 3.5in x12 no rear 3.5in x12 + 3.5in x4 mid + 3.5in x2 rear 3.5in x12 + 3.5in x4 mid + 2.5in x4 rear 3.5in x12 + 3.5in x2 rear 3.5in x12 + 2.5in x4 rear 2.5in x24 NVMe no rear 3.5in x12 Hybrid with NVMe U.2 no rear The 24-bay front takes ONE rear, the 4 x 2.5 inch, which figure 19 numbers 24-27. The 12-bay front takes either, and figure 19 numbers both from 12. This device carries the 24-bay front, which is why its rear reads 24-27. THE ARITHMETIC GOT THERE FIRST AND IS NOW REDUNDANT. Bays numbered 12-15 imply eleven bays this model does not have; that is how the error was found. Table 28 is how it is now SOURCED, and a guess agreeing with a document afterwards is worth more than either alone. THE RISER SIDE IS TABLE 25, and its discriminator is riser 2 rather than riser 3. Rear storage is offered in riser configurations 0, 1 and 2 and no others: 1 and 2 fit a one-slot low-profile riser 2 (2B or 2C, slot 4 only), while configuration 3 fits a three-slot 2A (slots 4, 5, 6) and has NO rear storage despite fitting no riser 3 at all. It is riser 2's full-height section that occupies the bay the rear cage needs. This device's configurations already encode exactly that - rear storage only with rc0, rc1 and rc2 - and row 3 is `rc3-1a2a`, added when the riser 3 opening and rear storage bay 3 turned out to be the SAME HOLE, closed by two different blanks depending on which configuration you picked. RE-READ AND STILL OPEN: that change touched which bay closes an opening, not the front-to-rear coupling this gap is about. Re-read again when riser 1's brackets moved 1 mm and slot 2 lost its numeral on 1A - both are ink and geometry inside one bay, and neither reaches across faces. Re-read a third time when riser 1's plate grew to meet the slot strip and the shroud: the bay's own box moved, and still nothing crossed a face. A fourth time when riser 2's three slots were aligned and its plate cut back to the full-height pair. That one surfaced a NEW question but not a new gap of this kind: a bay's occupant is drawn after the panel, so a card cannot be shown "only through its cutout" without a part drawn after the bays to mask it. Recorded where it belongs, on the riser 2 slot 6 cutout, rather than widened into this one. A fifth time when the screw tab was split out of the frame so it could draw in front of riser 2's bracket tails. That is a draw-order fact about one bay, not a coupling between faces. A sixth time when riser 3 became bay 1 reflected - mirrored brackets, a two-slot plate and its own slot strip. Handedness is a fact about one bay's own metal and reaches no further than that. A seventh time when riser 3 slid 9.525 right to sit over the power supply's edge. Moving one bay along its own face changes nothing about which front it can be sold with. An eighth time when two "rivet" pairs beside the divider turned out to be card retention clips. A misread of what is on the rear, corrected on the rear, and silent about any front. A ninth time when those rivets came back, scoped: they are what the riser cage mounts to and they show when drives are fitted instead. That one is a rear configuration telling two rear drawings apart, which is the mechanism this gap says is MISSING between faces - and still is. A tenth time when the C20 supply became its own part. A second occupant for an existing bay, on the same face, coupled to nothing at the front. TWO SOURCES DISAGREE AND ARE LEFT DISAGREEING. The system information label draws FIVE fronts - 24, 16 and 8 x 2.5 inch, 12 and 8 x 3.5 inch - where table 28 lists TWO front backplanes. Whether the 16- and 8-bay fronts are different chassis or one backplane drawn part-populated, nothing held here says. AND TABLE 28 HAS A MID DRIVE TRAY in three of its ten rows. This device models no mid bay at all, which is a whole third drive location missing rather than a detail.
gaps.wanted: NOW DEMONSTRABLE RATHER THAN HYPOTHETICAL. `rear-2-lff` draws a correct 2 x 3.5 inch rear on a 24 x 2.5 inch front, and ISM table 28 lists no such machine - every row carrying that rear has a 12-bay front. The mismatch even forced an id: the figure prints 12 and 13, which are already two of this chassis's front bays, so the rear ones had to be rear-drive-12 and rear-drive-13. An id clash is what this gap looks like from the inside. RE-READ AFTER THE REAR BAYS WERE SEPARATED, and still open. The rear half of this is now expressible: the chassis structure across bays 2 and 3 is its own always-present part, and what each bay holds - drives, PCIe, a blank - varies independently of the other. That was the piece `only-in` could not reach while one 287 mm component owned both bays. WHAT REMAINS IS THE FRONT. The 24 x 2.5 inch and 12 x 3.5 inch fronts are different panels, not different occupancy, and until the second is drawn nothing exercises the face-binding that would couple it to a rear. A way for a configuration to constrain more than one view at once. Today `only-in` scopes a bay to a configuration and every view chooses independently, so nothing stops a consumer selecting a 24-bay front and a rear numbered 12-15 - a machine that cannot be bought. The library needs either configurations that span views, or a declared incompatibility between them; and this device needs its 12 x 3.5 inch front modelled before either can be exercised, which is the same gap `rear-2-lff` already stands on.

a `power-draw-max-w` on each module this chassis accepts, from the vendor's own per-card table - Cisco publishes one per ambient, most vendors publish none, and until they land a module total is a floor

`cpu`, `memory` in a missing `attrs.platform` section; one of `power-max-w`, `power-max-ac-w`, `power-max-dc-w` in a missing `attrs.power` section; one of `operating-temp`, `operating-temp-f2b`, `operating-temp-b2f` in a missing `attrs.environmental` section (profile `server` - see spec/schemas/profiles.yaml) - unlocks the About panel, and comparison against other devices

bay-origin.note: THE ARRAY IS CENTRED, and that is a measurement rather than an assumption. ISM figure 2 puts the first release ring 35.27 mm from the left edge of the face and the last at 447.18, so the array runs 26.3..456.1 and leaves margins of 26.3 and 26.5 - symmetric to 0.15 mm. Implausibility is a failed check; symmetry here is the check passing. x is therefore (482.6 - 24 x 17.868)/2 = 26.884.

bay-pitch.note: 17.868 mm, read three times from three documents that agree to 0.05 mm: Dell's marketing render of this device (Gate 1 2.10%) gives 17.868; the r750-24d-2-5-front Visio master, a line drawing of the 15G successor that passes Gate 1 at 0.67%, gives 17.8454 across 23 gaps of exact vector coordinates; and ISM figure 2 at 600 dpi gives 17.9094 from the 24 orange release rings. The device's OWN source is kept - adopting a measurement of a different machine would trade provenance for false precision - and the other two are corroboration.

bay-vertical.note: drawing - the r750 master draws 22 of its 24 carriers with an identical outline at y 4.01..83.02, height 79.01 mm (bays 1 and 24 catch chassis paths and are excluded). Correcting the 0.7% by which that master draws the face 87.39 mm tall instead of 86.8 gives 78.48. common/drive-carrier-25 carries 79.4 from an independent source, and 0.5% agreement between a render and a line drawing is why that figure stands rather than being re-derived here.

bezel.note: DRAWN FITTED, AND IT DECLARES WHAT IT HIDES. `for:` names all 24 drive bays and the left control panel, which is how the C40G's snap-on PSU cover says it sits over four supplies - the same construction, and the reason L13 does not read a cover as a sizing mistake. A viewer can then hide it and see what is behind, which is the point. An earlier draft made it an `optional:` placement, the mechanism the SmartOptics rack ears use, and that was the wrong tool: `optional:` is for something absent unless asked for, and this is something PRESENT that a reader chooses to look past. IT CLEARS BOTH EARS AND DOES NOT COVER THE WHOLE FACE. At 434 x 82.35 centred on the 482.6 x 86.8 face it leaves 24.3 mm of ear showing each side and 2.2 above and below, which is the operator's description of where it sits and is what fixed its size - see dell/bezel-2u-14g, whose master aspect fails Gate 1 against a rack face precisely because a rack face is not what it covers.

chassis.note: datasheet - the R740xd spec sheet gives Height 86.8 mm, Width 434 mm, Depth 737.5 mm and notes the figures exclude the bezel. 434 is the BODY between the ear folds; the drawn front face is 482.6 because this device's ears carry ports (see front-face).

drive-default.note: EVERY BAY DEFAULTS TO A BLANK. A bay with nothing in it renders as an open hole, and a rack server does not ship with 24 open holes - it ships filled, because the airflow depends on it. Dell publishes no default drive count for this chassis, so the honest default is the filler rather than a drive count somebody invented. A populated machine is a configuration.

front-face.note: THE EARS ARE PART OF THE FACEPLATE AND CARRY PORTS, so they are drawn. Dell builds the mounting flanges into the front moulding and puts the VGA in the right-hand ear, the power button and USB stack in the strip beside it, and the system health lamp in the left. A 434 mm face would leave real, field-visible ports with nowhere to live. L43 tests what is seated in the outer 25 mm rather than the width, and passes this device for that reason.

gate-1.note: ISM figure 2 'Front view of 24 x 2.5 inch drive system', rendered from the PDF at 600 dpi, measures 3168 x 564 px on the chassis itself - aspect 5.6170 against 482.6/86.8 = 5.5599, which is 1.03%. ORTHOGRAPHIC, and at 6.5644 px/mm. An earlier reading of 12.16% measured the docling-EXTRACTED PNG, whose bounding box takes in the callout numerals and leader lines; extracting a figure and measuring a figure are not the same operation.

idrac-direct-led.note: A SEPARATE, UNMARKED LAMP BELOW THE PORT - not the wrench above it. That distinction is the document's own and it is worth spelling out, because two other glyph columns on this chassis work the other way: the drive carrier's head glyphs ARE its lamps and the left panel's five status glyphs ARE its lamps. Here ISM table 7 lists the iDRAC Direct PORT as item 3 with a wrench icon and the iDRAC Direct LED as item 4 with `Icon: N/A`, and figure 7's callout for item 4 points below the socket at plain strip. The wrench marks the hole; the lamp beneath it carries no mark at all. ITS CODES ARE SOURCED AND ITS PLACE IS APPROXIMATE, and those are not the same confidence. Table 8 gives all three codes. For the position the ISM says only "located below the iDRAC Direct port on the right control panel" and figure 7's callout agrees with that much; figure 2 at 6.5644 px/mm resolves the socket and the wrench above it and shows nothing beneath them, and figure 7 is schematic and carries no scale. So the 2.5 mm offset here is a sentence turned into a coordinate, and the size is common/led-dot's 2 mm, which that part itself calls estimated.

left-control-panel.note: photo-measured from ISM figure 2 at 6.5644 px/mm. NOT taken from the R750 master, which disagrees by 1.9 mm in x on the light bar and so is a different panel - the agreement that licensed the right-hand panel does not hold here, and reading it across anyway would have been the same evidence used twice with the negative result discarded.

not-yet-modelled.note: THIS IS A FRONT-FACE DRAFT AND SAYS SO. No rear view, no top view with the lid off, no riser configurations - the tech sheet documents twelve of those and they are the rear's business. The two control panels are drawn as their apertures and contents rather than as the field-replaceable units they are; the ISM has removal procedures for both, so each should become a component with its own bay, and the light bar in particular has no part in the library that fits it.

ports.note: POSITIONS from the figures above; SIZES from the registry. A connector's dimensions belong to spec/schemas/standards.yaml and to the std/ parts that conform to it, never to a reading of a picture - the picture is only allowed to say where the part sits.

power.note: NOT STATED HERE. The Information Update tech sheet (Rev 2, Nov 2022) lists thirteen orderable PSUs from 495 W to 2600 W across AC, DC, HVDC and Mixed Mode, so there is no single chassis figure to record; the draw belongs to whichever PSU is fitted, and that is a rear-face question this draft does not reach.

rack-latches.note: BOTH EARS CARRY ONE. The r750 master draws the same 12.16 x 37.99 section at x 2.80 and x 469.04, both starting at y 46.91 - 54% down an 86.8 face - and the operator describes the hardware the same way, "a little bit lower than midway down, and from there to the bottom". A drawing of the successor and a machine in a rack agreeing on where a feature starts is what fixed it. THE LEFT ONE IS CENTRED ON ITS EAR AND NOT ON THE MASTER'S x. The r750 draws it at x 2.80 in an ear of its own width; this chassis's left ear is 13.41 wide, so 2.80 put a 12.16 part 2.2 mm off centre and 1.55 mm past the ear's edge. A position read from another machine's drawing has to be re-seated against the metal it lands on - the master gives the part's SIZE, and the ear it sits in gives its PLACE. The right-hand one needed no such move: its ear runs 468.54..482.6 and the master's 469.04 already centres it there. An earlier reading took the right-hand one for the information tag. It is not: the ISM puts the information tag's callout in the middle of the drive row at the bottom, where it slides out from between the bays, and the tag is still not drawn.

right-control-panel.note: THE R740xd AND R750 SHARE THIS PANEL, which is what licenses reading exact vector geometry off the 15G master for a 14G machine, and it is established rather than assumed: the master puts the VGA at x 471.18..479.06 where the R740xd's own ISM figure puts it at 471.13..478.90 - 0.16 mm - and their power button centres agree to 0.5 mm. Where the two DISAGREE the ISM wins, because it is this device: the R750 carries one USB-A on this panel and the R740xd carries two, so the USB positions are the ISM's.

riser-configurations.note: THREE REARS ARE DRAWN AND THE MACHINE HAS FAR MORE THAN THREE. The Information Update tech sheet's table 3 enumerates TWELVE riser configurations - 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 9, 15, 16 and 17 - each naming which slots exist on risers 1, 2 and 3 and at what height and length: riser configuration 0 has no PCIe slots at all and only rear storage, 1 and 2 give four slots with or without it, 4 and 5 and 15 give eight. WHAT IS DRAWN HERE IS THE SHAPE OF THE ANSWER, not the whole of it. The three configurations modelled - no rear storage, four 2.5 inch rear, two 3.5 inch rear - establish that competing slot sets and drive bays are METAL scoped by `only-in` rather than different occupants of one hole. Extending that to twelve is transcription against table 3 and not a new mechanism; every slot already carries an id a configuration can name.

status-leds-are-dark-when-healthy.note: THE FIVE STATUS LAMPS HAVE EXACTLY TWO STATES AND THAT IS NOT A SHORTCUT. Dell publishes off and solid amber for each of drive, temperature, electrical, memory and PCIe, and nothing else: the ISM's own note above the table reads "The indicators display solid amber if any error occurs", every row says "turns solid amber", and the identical wording appears in the R740, R640, R750 and R760 manuals. Every occurrence of "blink" in this device's manual belongs to some other lamp - the health bar, Quick Sync, the NIC indicators or a PSU handle. SO DARKNESS IS THE HEALTHY STATE HERE, which is worth saying out loud because it is the opposite of most of this library: a dark lamp on this column means nothing is wrong, where a dark lamp on a line card usually means nothing is there.

y-correction.note: the ISM figure draws the face 85.8 mm tall where the datasheet says 86.8, so every y read off it is scaled by 1.0103. x needs no such correction: the figure's width matches 482.6 to the 1.03% that Gate 1 reports.
